sources.title: altNightHawk/Exfil_Server - Exfil Dedicated Server install script
install_exfil_server.sh - config paths and admin-role handling

notes: No command channel found. The Exfil dedicated server (Steam app 3093190; game app 860020, Tiny Leviathan, Early Access) publishes no RCON port, no admin HTTP/REST API and no documented console command set. The only server-side moderation surface found is on-disk JSON config in <install>/Exfil/Saved/ServerSettings/: AdminSettings.JSON carries AdminList entries ({steamId, name, adminLevel: "Admin"|"Moderator"}) and BanList entries ({steamId, name, banEnd} where banEnd is a "YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS" timestamp); ServerSettings.JSON (AutoStartTimer, MinAutoStartPlayers, AddAutoStartTimeOnPlayerJoin) and DedicatedSettings.JSON (MaxPlayerCount, ServerName, ServerPassword) hold the rest. Kick/ban in practice is done in-game by a player holding Admin/Moderator level, or by editing AdminSettings.JSON and restarting - neither is a command a manager can send. banList is omitted for SHAPE, not location: AdminList and BanList live in the same file, so a line-oriented lineIdPattern keyed on "steamId" would pull every admin Steam ID out of AdminList and report admins as banned, and banList has no way to scope a pattern to one JSON array. The path itself IS confirmed - install_exfil_server.sh sets ADMIN_SETTINGS_FILE=<user home>/exfil-dedicated/Exfil/Saved/ServerSettings/AdminSettings.JSON - correcting the earlier claim that it could not be found. The community installer exposes only a game port (7777) and a Steam query port (27015) - no RCON or web-admin port. The developer (IrOnTaXi) answers dedicated-server questions with "Jump in our discord and there is a section for people running servers" rather than published docs, so an admin command set may exist there undocumented; re-check if Tiny Leviathan publishes server documentation. Confidence is low: this rests on one community install-script repo plus the absence of any console/RCON mention on hosting-provider pages, not on publisher documentation.
